newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: F.J. Benjamin sees luxury retailing growth.
newsitem.headline: F.J. Benjamin sees luxury retailing growth.

text.p: Luxury goods sales have the potential for growth across Asia despite a general slowdown in other parts of the retail sector, the head of fashion retailor F.J. Benjamin said on Monday.
"There is no saturation point for luxury retailing in Singapore or Asia," Frank Benjamin told Reuters in an interview.

Benjamin, president and chief executive officer of the Singapore-based group, was also announcing the company's exclusive distribution rights for American designer label Isaac Mizrahi in Singapore, Hong Kong and Taiwan.
He said millions of people in Asia would be buying luxury goods as economies in the region became more affluent.
The general retail industry has faced tight margins over the last few years in parts of Asia, including Singapore, which some companies have blamed on high rents and overheads and sluggish demand.
Hong Kong's Lane Crawford, France's Galeries Lafayette and Kmart Corp of the United States have all closed their stores in Singapore in the past year.
Benjamin said retailers had to become more sophisticated to surf through the tougher times.
"Service will be paramount. Product knowledge and customer services as well. Singapore retailers have to develop these areas to stay on top," the founder of F.J. Benjamin said.
The main culprits for the slowdown in Singapore's retail sector were the softer yen and the strong Singapore dollar, he said.

"Singapore is suffering from a double-whammy. The retail market gets depressed when the yen weakens. More Singaporeans are getting better value overseas from the strong Singapore dollar compared to before," he said.
He dismissed reports that shopping in the island-state had become too expensive for residents.
"Together with Hong Kong, Singapore is still the cheapest place to shop in Asia (for luxury and fashion goods)," he said.
Benjamin was optimistic about Hong Kong's retail industry despite the British colony's return to Chinese rule in July.
"I am not worried about Hong Kong. Hong Kong will thrive. There will be hiccups but these will settle down," he said.
Asia would be one of the main expansion targets for the company, Benjamin said, noting that opportunities in Europe and America were looked at "conservatively".

F.J. Benjamin's distribution rights to the Isaac Mizrahi collection and its second line, IS**C, is for three years with effect from January 1, 1997. It includes Tiny Label and Tuxedo, Mizrahi's two new subdivisions.
The agreement includes two renewal periods of three years with an option to expand into Malaysia and Indonesia.
F.J. Benjamin planned to open at least nine Mizrahi boutiques in Singapore, Taiwan and Hong Kong over the next couple of years, Benjamin said.
